decisions.reason: NL2 requires activation following the listed collision detections. The exact model facts establish declared Collision_Detected consumers at transitions 12, 15, and 18, but the reachable consumer set is empty because Frontend and its operating leaves are unreachable from the top-level initial entry. Declaration-only consumers are a weaker property and do not rebut the reachable activation obligation.
decisions.violated_obligation: The three collision-detection stimuli must have an operational reachable path that activates CollisionAvoidanceSystem; the supplied reachable-consumer facts show none.

decisions.basis: Pair 0047 dossier: NL3 region-structure contract, exact CollisionAvoidanceSystem and child-state bindings, source inventory, and canonical concurrent-region count.
decisions.reason: NL3 requires orthogonal regions that permit concurrent activation of distinct controls. The exact canonical source/model facts report zero concurrent regions for CollisionAvoidanceSystem and represent Frontend, RearEnd, and Pedestrian as nested composites rather than typed concurrent regions. Their conceptual distinction does not establish the required orthogonal structure, so it is not a rebuttal.
decisions.violated_obligation: CollisionAvoidanceSystem must contain orthogonal concurrent regions for the distinct collision-avoidance controls, but the supplied structure contains no typed orthogonal regions.

decisions.basis: Pair 0047 dossier: NL1 cardinality contract, exact owner and child bindings, source inventory, canonical separator inventory, and finite region cardinality facts.
decisions.reason: NL1 says, in exact quotation, "There are three region in this diagram." Under the supplied primary concurrent_regions reading, the finite structure has one implicit UML region: no separator-derived region rows exist, and the three named direct children are not typed regions. A competent alternative remains because the wording can be read informally as counting the three named operating areas, while the supplied contract explicitly identifies concurrent_regions as the primary reading. Thus the first reading is established, but its scope is semantically undercut by the supported informal count reading.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The wording "There are three region in this diagram" can be read as an informal count of the three named areas Frontend, RearEnd, and Pedestrian rather than as a count of canonical UML concurrent regions.
decisions.violated_obligation: CollisionAvoidanceSystem must realize three regions under the primary canonical concurrent-region interpretation, but the supplied finite structure realizes one implicit region.

decisions.basis: Pair 0047 dossier: NL2 and NL3 contracts, exact Frontend binding, and finite root reachability result showing no path from the top-level initial source to Frontend behavior.
decisions.reason: The supplied contracts require Frontend to operate as part of collision-avoidance behavior, and the exact G1 result is false: the root source reaches UnspecifiedInitial, while the bound Frontend leaves Braking, Clamping, and Idle are absent from the reachable target set. Local declarations and transitions inside Frontend do not establish root reachability and therefore do not rebut this topology violation.
decisions.violated_obligation: The required Frontend operating scope must be reachable from the model root, but the exact finite reachability facts show that it is unreachable.

decisions.basis: Pair 0047 dossier: NL3 region-structure contract, exact RearEnd binding, and finite G1 reachability result with no root-to-RearEnd path.
decisions.reason: NL3 requires RearEnd to function as one of the collision-avoidance control areas. The exact G1 evaluation is false and its finite counterexample identifies only an invalid initial element under RearEnd rather than a reachable RearEnd target. No supplied fact establishes a root path to RearEnd; owner-local declarations cannot rebut failed root reachability.
decisions.violated_obligation: The required RearEnd operating scope must be reachable from the model root, but the exact finite graph facts show no such path.

decisions.basis: Pair 0047 dossier: NL3 region-structure contract, exact Pedestrian binding, and finite G1 reachability result with no root-to-Pedestrian path.
decisions.reason: NL3 requires Pedestrian to participate in the collision-avoidance control structure. The exact G1 evaluation is false, with the root source reaching UnspecifiedInitial and the bound Pedestrian target represented only by an invalid initial element outside the reachable set. The supplied dossier contains no exact root path or other behavior that would rebut this reachability failure.
decisions.violated_obligation: The required Pedestrian operating scope must be reachable from the model root, but the exact finite reachability facts show no such path.

decisions.basis: Pair 0047 dossier: NL2 activation contract, exact Frontend and Brake_Applied consumer bindings, and closed event-consumer facts showing declared but unreachable consumers.
decisions.reason: The dossier binds Frontend and its Brake_Applied consumer transitions exactly. The supplied event-consumer rows show declared consumers but an empty reachable_consumer_transition_refs set. Because the obligation is operational coverage, declaration alone is insufficient and does not rebut the established absence of a reachable consumer.
decisions.violated_obligation: Brake_Applied must have a reachable consumer within Frontend, but the exact event-consumer facts show that all declared consumers are unreachable.

decisions.basis: Pair 0047 dossier: NL2 source declarations, exact Idle binding, and closed PlantUML/model identity facts for the three enclosing blocks.
decisions.reason: The supplied source facts identify Idle declarations or entries at lines 4, 11, and 18 within Frontend, Pedestrian, and RearEnd. The exact closed-model facts state that PlantUML global state-name resolution collapses these declarations into one state, CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle, and that each default entry targets it. The possibility that the author intended independent local states is not supported by an exact source or model fact and therefore does not rebut the established identity collision.
decisions.violated_obligation: The three operating blocks require distinct Idle state identities, but the supplied PlantUML/model facts resolve the three declarations to one globally shared state.

issues.basis: NL2 and its transition group establish three required detection-triggered entries into the collision-avoidance sub-machine. The closed inventory and inspection-equivalent facts show CollisionAvoidanceSystem at state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:6, detection consumers at transition:line:12, transition:line:15, and transition:line:18, and no reachable consumer or target-entry transition for the required activation relation.
issues.expected: After any of the three collision-detection stimuli, the collision-avoidance sub-machine becomes active.
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidanceSystem is entered only by the untriggered top-level initial transition; the three detection-triggered transitions target Braking from Idle and are unreachable from the top-level initial entry. No exact activation consumer enters CollisionAvoidanceSystem.
issues.reason: The target collision-avoidance sub-machine is exact, but the complete closed transition inventory has no transition from an exact activation source to CollisionAvoidanceSystem carrying any of the three required detection stimuli. The only root entry reaches CollisionAvoidanceSystem without a trigger, and the detection-triggered transitions remain inside the unreachable Frontend state.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The required activation might be intended to occur through an enclosing or implicit event-routing mechanism not represented in the supplied closed FCSTM; no such mechanism or exact source transition is present in the supplied closure.
issues.title: Activation Consumers Do Not Enter Collision Avoidance

issues.basis: NL2; source transitions tr_0002, tr_0006, and tr_0010; closed event-consumer fact for Collision_Detected with consumer transitions transition:line:12, transition:line:15, and transition:line:18 and an empty reachable consumer set; reachability facts for Frontend, Idle, Braking, and Clamping; root reachability refs state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:6 and state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:35.
issues.expected: After any of the three specified collision-detection stimuli, the collision-avoidance sub-machine becomes active.
issues.observed: Collision_Detected has declared consumers, but none is reachable from the top-level initial entry; the only reachable child is UnspecifiedInitial, whose Collision_Avoided transition exits the composite.
issues.reason: The activation contract is behaviorally unmet in the reachable closed model. Collision_Detected is declared and has three exact consumer transitions, but all are unreachable because Frontend and its operating leaves are unreachable from the top-level initial entry. The top-level initial entry reaches CollisionAvoidanceSystem and then UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The three Collision_Detected consumer transitions are declared with the expected event, but this does not rebut the issue because the deterministic reachable-consumer set is empty.
issues.title: Required collision activation has no reachable consumer
